claim: How to move is one of three operations, the shuffle-diversity-redundancy (SDR) taxonomy, from Hong and Kim.
quote: We classify MTD techniques into three categories: (i) Shuffle, (ii) Diversity, and (iii) Redundancy.
locator: p. 163 printed (PDF p. 1), Sect. 1; also Sect. 2.3
issue: Hong and Kim classify MTD techniques into three categories; they do not frame them as answers to 'how to move' (that frame is Cho et al.'s, U0052), and the name 'SDR taxonomy' does not occur in the paper. The sentence joins two sources' framings under one citation.
fix_text: 'How to move is one of three operations, the shuffle--diversity--redundancy (SDR) taxonomy [hongkim2016]' -> 'How to move is one of three operations: shuffle, diversity and redundancy [hongkim2016]'

claim: (uncited neighbour, leans on hongkim2016) Shuffling rearranges or randomises existing components, such as addresses or links, so that the attacker's reconnaissance no longer holds.
quote: The Shuffle technique rearranges the system setting in various layers (e.g., address randomization, migration, topology rearrangements)
issue: The definition half matches Hong and Kim; the purpose clause 'so that the attacker's reconnaissance no longer holds' is not in hongkim2016. The unit carries no citation of its own.
fix_text: cite [hongkim2016] for the definition; source the reconnaissance clause elsewhere or mark it ours

claim: (uncited neighbour, leans on hongkim2016) Diversity replaces a component with a different implementation of the same function, so that an exploit against one no longer applies.
quote: The Diversity technique provides equivalent functions with different implementations
locator: p. 163 printed (PDF p. 1), Sect. 1; purpose clause p. 169 printed (PDF p. 7), Sect. 4.1
issue: Definition matches; the purpose clause matches Sect. 4.1 'forcing the attacker to use a different set of exploits for different vulnerabilities', which Hong and Kim qualify 'with an assumption of non-overlapping vulnerabilities'. Uncited, and the condition is dropped.
fix_text: cite [hongkim2016] at the end of the sentence
